newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 25.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- Cho Soon, mayor of Seoul will resign next month to run in the December presidential race as a third opposition candidate, a member of Congress for National Integration, a new opposition alliance, said on Thursday.

- Park Tae-joon, founder and former chariman of the Pohang Iron and Steel Co. (POSCO) won in the Pohang by-election and Oh Jang-sop, the ruling New Korea Party candidate, also won a parliamentary seat in Yesan's by-election.

- In a document submitted to Kia's main creditor Korea First Bank, all 21 top executives of the troubled group promised to resign if they should fail to put the group back on its feet, taking responsibility for the group's dire financial situation.
- South Korea and Russia agreed to set up a "hot-line" between Seoul's presidential Blue House and Moscow's Kremlin.
